title: Power Apps: prompt columns can store multiple lines of text output
summary: The page treats the cost effect of longer output as unpublished, although Microsoft's prompt billing documentation already counts output tokens. The roadmap facts and both UI controls are supported, with smaller corrections needed to clarify credit consumption and align the governance checklist with its table.

claims.claim: The prompt columns Learn page does not describe the planned multi-line output enhancement.
claims.quote: Searched: '"prompt columns" "multiple lines" output limit default existing credits' and '"prompt columns" "multi-line"'; opened the complete Prompt columns page, which describes general execution and other enhancements but not multi-line output.

claims.claim: How a maker chooses multi-line output is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse prompt columns multiple lines output default switch rollout existing columns'; opened Prompt columns and Specialized columns using code. Neither documents a selection mechanism for multi-line output.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The effect of the multi-line enhancement on existing prompt columns is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse prompt columns multiple lines output default switch rollout existing columns'; opened Prompt columns and Specialized columns using code. Existing-column upgrade text concerns asynchronous execution, not multi-line output.

claims.claim: A stored-output length limit for the planned multi-line prompt-column enhancement is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"prompt columns" output "length" limit' and '"prompt columns" "multiple lines" output limit default existing credits'; read Prompt columns and Specialized columns using code. General Multiline Text limits do not identify the planned prompt-column output limit.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state of the multi-line output enhancement is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse prompt columns multiple lines output default switch rollout existing columns'; read the roadmap record and Prompt columns. Defaults for execution and bulk processing are documented, but no default for multi-line output is stated.

claims.claim: No new admin switch specifically for multi-line prompt output is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse prompt columns multiple lines output default switch rollout existing columns'; opened Prompt columns, Administer AI Builder and Manage feature settings. Found general prompt controls, but no switch specific to multi-line output.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics for the multi-line output enhancement are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Dataverse prompt columns multiple lines output default switch rollout existing columns'; read the roadmap record and Prompt columns. The Learn rollout notes concern asynchronous execution and bulk backfill, not this multi-line enhancement.

claims.claim: The roadmap description names no new connector, identity or permission.
claims.quote: Prompt columns can now store multilple lines of text as prompt output, enabling longer and detailed AI-generated insights to be stored in your tables.

claims.claim: Insufficient permission on an input column is a documented cause of prompt-column generation failure.
claims.quote: The user doesn't have sufficient permissions on one or more input columns referenced in the prompt column definition.

claims.claim: Learn states that on-demand prompt-column execution is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Prompt columns are triggered automatically on record updates; however, on-demand execution is not currently supported.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Prompt columns use the consumption-based licensing model of AI Builder prompts.
claims.quote: Prompt columns use the same licensing model as AI builder prompts. Prompt columns consume credits every time a prompt is executed.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Prompt-column execution is credit-metered, with credits consumed each time a prompt runs.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume credits every time a prompt is executed. Copilot Credits are a common currency for eligible Microsoft services with usage-based billing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn says prompt columns consume both AI Builder credits and Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume both AI Builder credits and Copilot Credits.
claims.fix: Clarify the repeated wording so it does not imply both currencies are charged for every run: 'Prompt columns support AI Builder credits and Copilot Credits. General AI Builder licensing says features in apps and flows first consume AI Builder credits, then Copilot Credits if AI Builder credits are absent or exhausted.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/ai-builder/administer-licensing, which says 'AI Builder features in apps and flows first try to consume AI Builder credits, then if absent or exhausted, they try to consume Copilot Credits.'

claims.claim: The prompt columns page says AI Builder credits are retiring soon.
claims.quote: AI Builder credits are retiring soon.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Testing a prompt in the prompt designer is free.
claims.quote: In the prompt designer, select Test. Testing a prompt is free. The credits on lower right are estimates for one run.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The credit monitoring report is at Power Automate > Automation center > AI Builder activity.
claims.quote: Sign in to Power Automate. On the left navigation pane, select Automation center, and then select AI Builder activity.

claims.claim: The report's Estimated consumption column shows credits per prompt execution.
claims.quote: Review the Estimated consumption column to see the credits consumed by each prompt execution.

claims.claim: Filter conditions reduce unnecessary prompt executions and help optimize credit consumption.
claims.quote: During record creation or update, the prompt column evaluates the filter first and then executes the prompt for eligible records. This approach reduces unnecessary executions and helps optimize Copilot credit consumption.

claims.claim: The prompt columns prerequisites require the environment's Copilot feature to be on.
claims.quote: Copilot and AI Prompts features turned On in the Features area for the environment settings.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row; Open questions
claims.claim: An API or command for the environment AI prompts toggle is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'AI prompts environment setting disable API PowerShell Power Platform' and '"AI prompts" "Power Platform API" setting'; read Administer AI Builder, Set-PowerPlatformGenerativeAiSettings and Environment Management Settings - Update. No documented property sets this toggle.

claims.claim: An AI prompts environment group rule can govern AI prompts availability for environments in that group.
claims.quote: If your environment is part of an environment group, you can also govern AI prompts feature availability through the AI prompts environment group rule.

claims.claim: Publishing an AI prompts group rule locks the environment setting, so changes must be made through the group rule.
claims.quote: If an environment group rule governing AI prompts is published, it locks the AI prompts setting at the environment-level, preventing any system administrator of those individual environments from editing the setting.

claims.claim: The per-column execution control is at Power Apps > Tables > table > Columns > column > Allow prompt column execution.
claims.quote: Open the table, select Columns, and then open the column that is of data type Prompt where you want to disable AI generation. On the Edit column pane, clear the Allow prompt column execution checkbox, and then select Save.
claims.fix: Include the omitted pane heading in the front matter and rendered row: 'Tables > table > Columns > column > Edit column > Allow prompt column execution'. The cited page identifies Edit column as the pane containing the checkbox.

claims.claim: Allow prompt column execution is enabled by default.

claims.claim: Clearing Allow prompt column execution prevents AI analysis for that column.

claims.claim: Learn states that both tenant-level and column-level settings must be enabled for prompts to execute.

claims.claim: Learn does not specifically tie the two general prompt controls to the multi-line output enhancement.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Whether longer multi-line output changes the credits consumed per run is not yet published.
claims.quote: The combination of input tokens, output tokens, and the model version allows you to compute the cost of your prompt run.
claims.fix: Replace the cost paragraph's final absence with: 'Prompt-run cost depends on input tokens, output tokens and the model version; longer generated output can therefore increase consumption.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/ai-builder/licensing-prompt-tokens. In the cost rationale, replace 'Microsoft has not published whether multi-line output changes that consumption' with 'prompt-run cost depends on input tokens, output tokens and the model version'. Remove 'and does longer output change the credits per run?' from Open questions. A separate rate specific to multi-line storage may remain an open question, but the general effect of generated output tokens is already documented.

claims.claim: Prompt execution consumes the environment's available AI credit capacity.
claims.quote: Once an environment has Copilot Credits available, it can run the AI Builder features in all contexts. If an environment only has AI Builder credits available, it can only run AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/ai-builder/administer-licensing to sources for the environment credit-capacity statement and the credit-consumption qualification.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist names monitoring controls that have no corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: 'Add the Status and Details columns for each prompt column to a view' and 'Review the AI Builder activity report' appear in the checklist; the table contains only the environment AI prompts and per-column execution controls.
claims.fix: The Status/Details monitoring step and the AI Builder activity report review step have no controls-table rows. Keep those sentences as monitoring advice outside the governance checklist so the checklist matches the existing table; no additional control rows are required for this correction.
